lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The $0.63 Q2 EPS bar looks set too low. For Q1, management used the identical guidance wording ('net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower year over year'). Consensus then sat at $0.41-0.43 against $0.56 a year earlier, and Q1 printed $0.57, flat. Q2 consensus now sits 36% below last year's $0.98. Starting from Q1's segment EBITDA of $32.3m ($0.57), Q2's seasonal segment margins (Q2 FY26: Metals 14.8%, Glass 16.1%, Performance Surfaces 23.2%, after cutting Glass to Q1's ~9%) plus two months of Kalwall (~$85m a year at ~15% EBITDA) give roughly $0.68-0.88.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26): $0.57 vs $0.41-0.43 with the guide reaffirmed, +15.2%. Q4 FY26 (2026-04-24): beat with an FY27 guide below FY26, +7.6%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09): $0.98 vs $0.86 but the FY guide cut, -4.4%. So beats pay when the guide holds.

findings.finding: The guide is H2-weighted on 'anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions', and the AIA/Deltek ABI says that improvement has not started. The August ABI was 47.2, contracting in 46 of the last 47 months, and firms expecting Q4 2026 billings to rise fell from 31% to 25% while those expecting declines rose from 21% to 29%. That raises the risk of a guide narrowed to the low end or cut, partly offset by two acquisitions that raise the sales guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts were sold hard: 2026-01-07 (FY guide 6% below estimates) -13.9%; 2025-01-07 -19.0%; 2025-10-09 FY26 guide lowered despite a beat, -4.4%. Reaffirmation on 2026-06-26 was bought (+15.2%).

findings.finding: Aluminum input costs kept rising through Apogee's Jun-Aug quarter. Tecnoglass cut its 2026 EBITDA guide on 2026-08-06, citing all-in US aluminum up ~77% year on year and ~$17m of Section 232 cost in one quarter. That is a lagged pass-through risk to Architectural Metals (~37% of sales).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metals margin drove the FY26 tariff-driven guide cuts (the Oct 2025 and Jan 2026 prints, -4.4% and -13.9%). In Q1 FY27 Metals margin rose +390bps on pricing and surcharges and the stock rose 15.2%.

findings.finding: GroGlass (Latvia, anti-reflective glass coatings, ~$30m revenue at ~25% adjusted EBITDA margin, about €62.5m plus up to €10m earnout, ~9-10x EBITDA, funded from cash and the revolver) closed 2026-09-23. Management said financial details would come on this Q2 call, so the sales guide rises again (Kalwall already took it to $1.43-1.48bn), and the deal buys a margin above Apogee's own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Kalwall announcement and Q1 together drew +15.2% on 2026-06-26, but on Kalwall's closing (07-01 to 07-02) the stock fell ~7.6% as leverage worries surfaced (~2x pro forma).

lessons_applied: Rule 5 / core 'inference smaller': the Q2 beat finding rests on a seasonality model and a wording pattern, not a reported number, so it was trimmed from +4.0 to +3.5 and print_vs_bar from +18 to +15.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): GroGlass revolver funding buys a 25%-margin business, so it stays signed small positive at +0.3.

findings.finding: Raw materials re-inflated after RPM set its guide. RPM guided on 07-22, when oil was back at pre-war levels (late June). Brent then rose to about $113 on 09-09 on renewed Hormuz attacks, and North American MDI rose 5.6% and PU 9% in September. That threatens the Q2 outlook RPM gives on this call (it had already said Q2 raw inflation 6-8%) and the 'moderating in H2' assumption under the FY +5-10% EBITDA guide. Netted against an ~18% de-rating since August while estimates stayed flat, this is a small negative.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold or ignored: Q3 FY26 (2026-04-01) beat EPS by $0.09 and raised the FY midpoint, -8.94%. Q4 FY26 (2026-07-24) beat above the top of guide, +0.81%. Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30) beat and reaffirmed, +4.33%.

findings.finding: Europe's 2026 crop has turned from the 'average crop' and 'favorable start' management described on 2026-07-24 into the smallest in decades. EU-4 output is ~20.8 Mt, down ~24% y/y, with yields 7-21% below the 5-year average. Belgian/Dutch free-buy processing potatoes have gone from ~EUR 0-15/t in spring to EUR 200-275/t. Management had also flagged a 'more pronounced reduction in contracted volumes', and the 2026 contracts were set 15-25% lower. The EMEA cost for FY27 Q2-Q4 is therefore above what the July guide assumed ('inflation in all inputs other than raw potatoes'). Net of the offset (a short crop ends the EMEA overcapacity price war that took International EBITDA down 81% in Q4, and competitors Clarebout and Lutosa are cutting shifts), the sign leans negative for the guide and the call tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and EMEA lines have moved this stock the most. Dec 2025 (Q2: H2 margins flat to down, EMEA curtailed): -25.94%. Dec 2024 (guide cut): -20.10%. Oct 2025 Q1, guide reaffirmed despite EMEA pressure: +4.33%.

findings.finding: North American crop since July: Idaho yields are down up to 20% y/y on drought and heat, with smaller tubers, and Lamb Weston is named as receiving smaller tubers from affected growers. The Columbia Basin is reported as average and on par with 2025. In July management said the NA crop was off to a 'strong start' with contracted acreage modestly higher. The new crop is processed from Q2 onward, so lower recovery from small tubers raises cost. A smaller Idaho crop also trims industry oversupply, which supports the 'LSD price/mix decline' assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Crop-driven guide changes have historically come at the December (Q2) print once the crop is in storage (Dec 2024 -20.1%, Dec 2025 -25.9%). At the October print the guide was reaffirmed (Oct 2025 +4.3%).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is at peak caution. Put/call is 2.08, level with its 52-week high and >2 SD above average. JPM ($46) and Stephens ($50) cut targets in the week before. The stock is -10.6% over 20 days and -33% from its 52-week high. Short interest is modest at 4.7%. A Q1 print that lands on guide and reaffirms FY27, which is what LW did at the last Q1 (Oct 2025, +4.33%), meets hedged rather than long positioning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30), guide reaffirmed after a weak run-in: +4.33%. Q4 FY26 after a strong run-up: +0.81%.

findings.finding: US QSR traffic, LW's largest channel, is weak. McDonald's US foot traffic has declined y/y in every complete month since March (Placer.ai): -3.1% in the week of Sept 7 against -2.8% for all QSR, and McDonald's Q2 US comps were +0.8%. That threatens the FY27 'low single-digit volume growth' assumption for North America. LW's share wins (+11% NA volume in Q4) cushion it.
